svg.text: Beaver's Choice Paper Company: Multi-Agent Workflow
Orchestrator + 3 worker agents (4 of the 5 allowed). Each tool is labelled with the starter-code helper function it wraps.
Parses request into items, quantities, deadline, request date
Runs workers in order: Inventory, then Quoting, then Sales
Fulfils lines that can ship on time; rejects the rest with reasons
Writes the customer reply (no margins, errors or personal data)
Role: map customer wording to catalog item names, check
stock, decide what to restock; verify cash and delivery time
Out: fulfillable lines, restock ETA, rejected lines + reasons
Role: price the fulfillable lines, apply a bulk discount
and explain how the price was reached
Out: itemised quote with discount rationale
Role: finalize the order when feasible, otherwise decline
with a clear reason (not in catalog, low stock, too late)
Out: order confirmation or rejection with reason
Map customer wording to the exact catalog item name
Helper: none (fuzzy match on the paper_supplies list)
Stock on hand, shortfall and how much to restock
Everything in stock; flags low-stock items
Will a restock arrive before the customer deadline?
Confirm we can afford a restock (keeps a cash reserve)
Buy stock from the supplier (cash goes down)
Pull past quotes for pricing and wording style
Get the catalog price per unit
Price the order and apply the tiered bulk discount
Review cash and assets before large orders
Record the sale (cash up); refuses if stock is too low
Tables: transactions (stock and sales ledger) | inventory | quotes | quote_requests
Workers never call each other: the orchestrator passes each result to the next agent. Solid two-way arrows = delegate and return results.
Date rule: every tool receives the request date (YYYY-MM-DD) so stock, cash and delivery times match the day of the request.
